(3) A concrete valid negative audience consists of a live nonretired target S with N completed join/leave episodes on thread T before warning W's recipient cutoff, no service notification or warning_recipients entry for (W,S), and W affecting another seat. The schema permits arbitrary distinct positive episodes (migrations/0001_initial.sql:249-260). (4) W is nevertheless visited by the global warning source (queries.rs:7008-7025). is_warning_recipient tests service/projected recipients, obtains canonical high_water/cutoff, and bypasses the affected-seat shortcut for S (effective.rs:1600-1649). Its actual fallback (:1650-1655) is EXISTS over membership_intervals with thread/seat equality, ordinal<=high, joined_seq<=cutoff and residual (left_seq IS NULL OR left_seq>cutoff). Every one of S's N older closed intervals satisfies the indexed prefix/ranges but fails that residual. The installed full indexes are thread/ordinal, thread/seat/joined_seq, the UNIQUE thread/seat/episode index (0001:249-260), and thread/seat/ordinal (0045_presentation_relevance.sql:93). None indexes left_seq for closed intervals. The open partial index excludes those rows and cannot prove absence of a qualifying closed interval. SQLite's primary optimizer documentation, fetched at https://www.sqlite.org/optoverview.html, says: 'The right-most column that is used can employ inequalities.' Its partial-index documentation, fetched at https://www.sqlite.org/partialindex.html, says: 'Only rows of the table for which the WHERE clause evaluates to true are included in the index.' With the shipped query/index shapes, determining this negative EXISTS requires inspecting the retained matching closed-history range; changing N changes that physical work without changing the number of warning candidates. This is a structural scaling demonstration, not a measured latency or specific chosen-plan claim.
